packages.title: SECR 2026 PIR administrative-burden QA
facts: The 2026 SECR review considers whether the framework could be simplified or improved to reduce administrative burden.
Administrative burden is a policy-evaluation metric rather than an emissions quantity.
The review also considers alignment with wider corporate reporting requirements.
Potential simplification does not alter already reported emissions data by itself.
No parcel value is inferred from regulatory-burden findings.

packages.title: RPC SECR PIR fit-for-purpose QA
facts: The Regulatory Policy Committee rated the SECR post-implementation review fit for purpose.
The rating concerns the quality of evidence and analysis supporting the review.
It is not a rating of any individual company's emissions data.
A regulatory-review opinion must not be interpreted as a measurement-quality certificate for a parcel.
No emissions value is inferred from the RPC rating.

packages.title: Public-sector sustainability Scope 1-2 materiality QA
facts: HM Treasury sustainability reporting guidance includes minimum requirements for domestic Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and applies materiality considerations to additional sustainability information.
Scope 1 and Scope 2 are reporting categories with different boundaries.
Materiality decisions concern reporting relevance rather than physical parcel geometry.
Public-sector reporting requirements are not direct site-sensor measurements.
No parcel emissions are inferred from reporting materiality.

packages.title: SHDF 149,400 measures installed QA
facts: The June 2026 SHDF release reports around 149,400 measures installed across Waves 1, 2.1 and 2.2 to the end of April 2026.
The figure is scheme delivery activity.
Installed measures are not a measured GHG total.
The release covers England and uses grant-recipient returns.
No parcel emissions are inferred from measure counts.

packages.title: SHDF 68,600 households upgraded QA
facts: The June 2026 SHDF release reports around 68,600 households upgraded across the covered waves to the end of April 2026.
Households upgraded and measures installed are distinct counts.
A household count does not specify energy saved or emissions avoided for each dwelling.
Scheme statistics are provisional and subject to revision.
No parcel GHG value is derived from the household count.

packages.title: SHDF Wave 2.1 108,100 measures QA
facts: SHDF Wave 2.1 had delivered around 108,100 measures by the end of April 2026.
The same release reports around 48,200 households upgraded under Wave 2.1.
Measures and households use different denominators.
Delivery activity is not the same as operational emissions performance.
No parcel value is inferred from Wave 2.1 totals.

packages.title: SHDF Wave 2.2 9,600 measures QA
facts: SHDF Wave 2.2 had installed around 9,600 measures by the end of April 2026.
The release reports around 4,300 households upgraded under Wave 2.2.
Wave totals must remain separated from other SHDF waves.
Installation activity is not direct energy or GHG measurement.
No parcel value is assigned from Wave 2.2 totals.

packages.title: SHDF EPC C denominator QA
facts: The SHDF June 2026 summary reports very high shares of known pre/post EPC cases reaching EPC C or above for Waves 2.1 and 2.2.
Those percentages apply only where the required EPC information is known and the initial rating met the stated condition.
The known-EPC denominator is smaller than all upgraded households.
EPC band improvement is not direct operational emissions measurement.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from the EPC percentage.

packages.title: SHDF two-month reporting lag QA
facts: SHDF monthly statistics are reported with a two-month lag.
The June 2026 publication covers installations to the end of April 2026.
Publication month and activity month must not be conflated.
Lagged scheme reporting may later be revised.
No current-month parcel activity is inferred beyond the reporting cutoff.

packages.title: SHDF provisional revision QA
facts: SHDF monthly figures are provisional and subject to future revision.
Grant-recipient returns can be updated after initial publication.
A provisional count must not be labelled final.
Revision status is part of the source provenance.
No parcel emissions are inferred from a provisional scheme count.

packages.title: SHDF previous-month revision contribution QA
facts: The June 2026 SHDF summary states most of the increase in Wave 2.1 measures and households versus the prior release came from net upward revisions to earlier months.
This demonstrates that publication-to-publication changes need not equal newly completed activity in the latest month.
Revision effects and new delivery must remain separate.
A change in published totals is not automatically a physical emissions change.
No parcel value is inferred from revision deltas.

packages.title: Warm Homes Social Housing Fund 4,850 measures QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:SHF detail reports around 4,850 measures reported by grant recipients to the end of May 2026.
The statistic measures reported scheme activity.
Measure counts do not equal carbon savings or measured emissions.
The scheme applies to social housing in England.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from the measure count.

packages.title: Warm Homes Social Housing Fund 2,600 homes QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:SHF detail reports around 2,600 households associated with the reported measures to the end of May 2026.
Households and measures are separate metrics.
The number of households does not provide a per-home emissions value.
Figures are provisional and expected to be revised.
No parcel measurement is inferred.

packages.title: WH:SHF 41 of 138 grant recipients reporting QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:SHF publication is based on returns from 41 of 138 participating grant recipients by mid-June 2026.
The reporting coverage is incomplete.
Coverage must be preserved when interpreting totals.
An incomplete reporting base cannot be silently treated as full scheme activity.
No missing activity or parcel emissions are fabricated.

packages.title: WH:SHF under-reporting caution QA
facts: DESNZ states early WH:SHF figures are likely to significantly under-report actual activity because of grant-recipient reporting issues.
The published figures are still an accurate representation of returns received at the cutoff.
Under-reporting uncertainty must be stated rather than corrected by guesswork.
Scheme activity uncertainty is not a basis for estimating parcel emissions.
No missing measures are invented.

packages.title: Warm Homes Local Grant 4,730 measures QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:LG publication reports around 4,730 measures from the start of delivery through the end of May 2026.
The figure is reported programme activity in England.
Measures installed are not direct GHG measurements.
Publication figures are provisional.
No parcel emissions are inferred from measure counts.

packages.title: Warm Homes Local Grant 2,470 households QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:LG publication reports around 2,470 households with reported measures to the end of May 2026.
Household count and measure count must remain distinct.
The publication does not establish measured GHG emissions for those households.
Regional shares have different underlying populations and participation.
No parcel GHG value is inferred.

packages.title: WH:LG 50 of 74 grant recipients reporting QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:LG publication is based on returns from 50 of 74 participating grant recipients by mid-June 2026.
Incomplete reporting coverage can understate scheme activity.
Published totals must retain the reporting-coverage caveat.
Missing grant-recipient data are not imputed as parcel emissions.
No unreported measures are fabricated.

packages.title: WH:LG 30 July future-release guard QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:LG detail states the next publication is scheduled for 30 July 2026.
At the current 25 July 2026 date that release remains in the future.
Future publication values must not be treated as observed data.
The latest usable release remains the June 2026 publication for this QA batch.
No future scheme figures are fabricated.
